q: Match the phase of parturition with what characterises it — 1) Phase 1, uterine quiescence 2) Phase 2, myometrial activation 3) Phase 4 … A) The postpartum phase B) Unresponsive uterus, soft cervix, progesterone the main hormone C) Functional progesterone withdrawal with cervical ripening
exp: Phase 1 is quiescence with an unresponsive uterus, soft cervix and progesterone dominant; phase 2 is activation with functional progesterone withdrawal, more oxytocin and prostaglandin receptors, more gap junctions and cervical ripening; phase 4 is the postpartum phase.

q: All of the following occur in phase 2 of parturition, the myometrial activation phase, EXCEPT:
opts: Functional withdrawal of progesterone with a rise in estrogen
More oxytocin and prostaglandin receptors with more gap junctions
exp: Phase 2 is functional withdrawal of progesterone, a rise in estrogen, more oxytocin and prostaglandin receptors, more gap junctions and cervical ripening — not a rise in progesterone action.

q: All of the following are among the five criteria for normal labour EXCEPT:
opts: Delivery by caesarean section if the labour becomes prolonged
Term gestation, that is 37 to 42 completed weeks
Vertex presentation with an uncomplicated vaginal delivery
exp: The five criteria are spontaneous onset, term gestation (37-42 weeks), vertex presentation, uncomplicated delivery and vaginal delivery.

q: Fill up: The fetal cascade for the onset of labour runs from fetal hypothalamic ______ to pituitary ACTH to fetal adrenal ______ and then to placental estrogen.
exp: The cascade is hypothalamic CRH, pituitary ACTH, fetal adrenal DHEA-sulfate, conversion to estrogen in the placenta and then uterine contractions.

q: Fill up: Lightening is descent of the fetal head into the pelvis, which causes a ______ in fundal height and relieves ______.
exp: Lightening is descent of the head into the pelvis, lowering the fundal height and relieving respiratory distress.

q: Which statement about cervical ripening before labour is TRUE?
opts: Ripening reduces cross-linking of fibres and raises water content and hyaluronic acid
Ripening increases cross-linking and reduces water content and hyaluronic acid
Ripening increases collagen deposition and reduces the water content
Ripening increases elastin and reduces the amount of hyaluronic acid
exp: Ripening is due to prostaglandins and connective-tissue change: less cross-linking of fibres, more water content and more hyaluronic acid.

q: Which statement about true versus false labour pain is TRUE?
opts: True labour contractions are regular and progressive in strength; false labour pains are neither
True labour contractions are irregular and continuous; false labour pains are regular and rhythmic
True labour contractions continue at a fixed intensity; false labour pains are rhythmic and progressive
True labour contractions are regular but decreasing; false labour pains are progressive and rhythmic
exp: True labour contractions are regular and increase in frequency, duration and intensity; false labour pains do neither.

q: Match the feature of labour with the type of labour it belongs to — 1) Site of the pain 2) Show and bag of membranes 3) Response to sedation, enema and rest … A) Relieved by sedation in false labour, not relieved in true labour B) Lower abdomen radiating to the back of the thigh in true labour C) Show present and membranes felt in true labour
exp: True labour pain is in the lower abdomen radiating to the back of the thigh, the show is present and the bag of membranes is felt, and it is not relieved by sedation; false labour does not radiate, has no show, and is relieved by sedation, enema and rest.

q: Fill up: In true labour the show is ______ and the bag of membranes ______; in false labour neither is found.
exp: In true labour the show is present and the bag of membranes is felt; in false labour the show is absent and the membranes are not felt.

q: Fill up: False labour pains are ______ by sedation, enema and rest, whereas true labour pains are ______.
exp: False labour pains respond to sedation, enema and rest; true labour pains do not.

q: Fill up: The three Ps required for labour are ______, ______ and ______.
exp: The 3 Ps are Push, meaning uterine contractions, Passage, meaning the pelvis, and Passenger, meaning the baby.

q: Match each feature of uterine contractions with its value — 1) Origin 2) Speed of spread 3) Time to depolarise the whole uterus 4) Predominant site … A) 2 cm per second B) Fundus C) Cornua D) 15 seconds
exp: Contractions originate in the cornua, spread at 2 cm per second, take 15 seconds to depolarise the entire uterus, and are predominant at the fundus.

q: Fill up: The commonest cause of breech overall is ______, and of recurrent breech is ______.
exp: The commonest cause of breech overall is prematurity, since spontaneous rotation has not yet occurred, and of recurrent breech is uterine malformation.

q: Match the breech type with what is felt on vaginal examination — 1) Complete breech 2) Frank breech 3) Knee presentation 4) Footling breech … A) Anus and ischial tuberosities B) Heel, anus and ischial tuberosities C) Feet D) Knees
exp: The more the legs are extended, the less is felt: complete breech gives the heel, anus and tuberosities, frank breech the anus and tuberosities, knee presentation the knees, and footling breech the feet.

q: Fill up: Complete breech is the ______ common breech overall, but the commonest breech in a ______.
exp: Complete breech is the least common breech overall and the commonest in a multigravida; frank breech is the commonest overall and in a primigravida.

q: Which statement about cord-prolapse risk in breech is TRUE?
opts: Risk rises as the presenting part fits the cervix less well, so frank is lowest and footling highest
The risk of cord prolapse is identical for all four types of breech
Frank breech carries the highest risk and footling breech the lowest
Complete breech carries the highest risk and frank breech the lowest
exp: Cord prolapse risk rises as the presenting part fits the cervix less well: frank breech is snug and lowest, complete is low, knee is higher and footling is highest.

q: Fill up: Overall cord-prolapse risk ranks ______ above footling breech above knee presentation, and the commonest breech position is ______.
exp: Cord prolapse risk ranks transverse lie above footling breech above knee presentation, and the commonest breech position is dorso-anterior.

q: A woman at 38 weeks is found to have a breech presentation and external cephalic version is being considered. What must ultrasound rule out before the version is attempted?
opts: Gross congenital anomalies, hyperextension of the fetal neck and a weight of 4 kg or more
Placenta previa, oligohydramnios and a single loop of cord
Cord presentation, vasa previa and a velamentous insertion
Fetal hydrocephalus, duodenal atresia and bilateral renal agenesis
exp: Ultrasound looks for the three findings that contraindicate external cephalic version: gross anomalies, a stargazer (hyperextended) neck and an estimated fetal weight of 4 kg or more.

q: A woman at 38 weeks with an uncomplicated breech has an external cephalic version in the OPD. The version succeeds and the cardiotocograph afterwards is reassuring. What happens next?
opts: Send her home to await spontaneous labour; labour is not induced
Induce labour immediately with an oxytocin infusion
Book an elective caesarean section for 39 weeks regardless
Repeat the version later the same day to confirm it holds
exp: After a successful version the woman goes home to labour and is not induced; a failed attempt is retried, and any fetal distress ends the attempt and prompts delivery.

q: Which statement about the mode of delivery in breech is TRUE?
opts: Caesarean section is strongly preferred over assisted breech delivery
Assisted breech delivery is strongly preferred over caesarean section
Breech extraction is the preferred mode of delivery in all cases
Caesarean section and assisted breech delivery are equally preferred
exp: Caesarean section is strongly preferred over assisted breech delivery in breech presentation.

q: Fill up: In breech labour, a protracted active phase is treated as ______ and is managed by ______.
opts: Uterine inertia; artificial rupture of membranes
exp: Delay in the first or second stage of breech labour is treated as cephalopelvic disproportion and managed by immediate caesarean section.
